Diego Martinez: Share benchmark spreadsheet and request sample payloads (due 2026-03-09)

Latency vs cost and batching/quantization options
summary: Discovery call to understand Aquila Dynamics' use case for an LLM-powered assistant, evaluate Redwood PLG quickstart, clarify security/VPC needs, and plan benchmarks. Customer is interested in fast time-to-first-token via self-serve, but needs enterprise security for production. Agreed to share pricing, security docs, free credits, and schedule SE demo/benchmarks.
transcript:
[00:00] Sophie Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Sophie from Redwood, I have Diego from our SE team with me. Quick introductions?
[00:12] Liam O'Connor: Hi, Liam here, CTO at Aquila Dynamics. We've got Priya, our ML lead, and Marco from infra.
[00:18] Priya Shah: Hey all.
[00:20] Marco Ruiz: Hi.
[00:22] Sophie Chen: Awesome. The goal for today is a quick PLG quickstart discovery — get an idea of your eval goals, timeline, and any blockers like VPC, compliance, or latency SLOs, and then we'll outline next steps. Does that sound right?
[00:32] Liam O'Connor: Yep, that's perfect. We looked at your quickstart page and the free credits, want to see how fast Priya can get to first token and then plan a mini POC.
[00:40] Diego Martinez: Cool. Just to set expectations: the quickstart should get you to first token within minutes for a basic text generation call — assuming you use the hosted API and our sample SDK. If you need Dedicated or Private we can spin up reserved pools but that takes longer, obviously.
[00:54] Priya Shah: Two quick things: 1) Data sensitivity — we'll likely send customer logs and some PII-ish telemetry to the model, so we need encryption + KMS and audit logs. 2) Latency SLOs: we need 95th percentile < 200ms for a majority of calls, but we can batch some low-priority stuff.
[01:12] Sophie Chen: Great notes. We support KMS integrations for key management and we retain audit logs — I'll share the SOC2 and security whitepaper after this call. For latency 200ms at p95 is ambitious on very large models on hosted, but for smaller quantized variants or using Dedicated pools we can get closer — Diego can talk through kernel/quantization and batching tradeoffs.
[01:33] Diego Martinez: Yeah, so the tradeoffs are classic: Hosted on the broad pool gives fastest start and lower ops burden but your p95 will depend on queueing and our batching. Dedicated gives predictable tail latency since you have reserved GPU capacity and locality; Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you full network control but requires provisioning time and you'll manage infra. Also note, KV cache/prefix caching helps a lot for repeated prompts.
[01:55] Marco Ruiz: For Private we need to know if you support our EKS setup and CNI specifics; we run in a VPC with private subnets and strict egress rules. Can Redwood Private be air-gapped?
[02:07] Diego Martinez: We have an on-prem package that can be operated in air-gapped environments; there are extra steps and a longer lead time. For VPC deployments we have connectors and documented EKS patterns, will share a reference runbook.
[02:20] Liam O'Connor: On the cost side, how do committed Dedicated contracts compare to hosted pay-as-you-go? We're trying to model expected token spend.
[02:28] Sophie Chen: Short answer: hosted is per-token and is great for PLG/self-serve early adoption. Dedicated is a commit with lower unit cost for sustained production traffic. I'll include an example TCO spreadsheet in the follow-up.
[02:39] Priya Shah: Are there any limitations around function calling or streaming in the quickstart flow? We rely on streaming for our UI.
[02:46] Diego Martinez: Streaming is supported in hosted quickstart and SDKs — it's in the docs. Function/tool calling works, but if you need guaranteed throughput for streaming we'd recommend Dedicated. In hosted, streaming is best-effort depending on load.
[03:00] Speaker 2 (automated): [transcription gap]...
[03:04] Marco Ruiz: Another infra question: what about egress/data residency? Some of our EU customers require data to stay in eu-west regions.
[03:13] Sophie Chen: We can pin region routing for requests and we have EU regions. We'll include the routing/regions doc.
[03:20] Liam O'Connor: Wanted to ask about security certifications — SOC2, ISO?
[03:25] Sophie Chen: We are SOC2 Type II, and we have ISO in progress. I'll share the compliance pack.
[03:31] Priya Shah: For the benchmarks — Diego, can you run a sample throughput test with our prompt set? We have ~1.2k token average and need to estimate concurrency.
[03:42] Diego Martinez: Yep, that works. If you can share a representative prompt batch and expected concurrency, I can run it on a Dedicated staging pool and share a benchmark sheet. For quickstart you can try the hosted flow to validate functional behavior first — it won't reflect dedicated tail latency.
[03:58] Priya Shah: Cool. We'll provide sample prompts and an expected concurrency profile.
[04:02] Marco Ruiz: About SSO / SAML and RBAC: we need role separation for dev vs prod. Does Redwood support org-level RBAC and SAML provisioning?
[04:11] Sophie Chen: Yes, SSO via SAML/SCIM and org RBAC are supported for Dedicated and Hosted enterprise orgs. For PLG/self-serve you can still do API keys for early tests; SSO comes with the enterprise onboarding.
[04:25] Liam O'Connor: Any mention of competitors? Some folks on our side tried Anthropic and OpenAI — curious how Redwood differs for serving and ops.
[04:34] Diego Martinez: Our differentiation is production-first serving: predictable inference knobs (batching, cache, quantization), dedicated pools, and a control plane that works across hosted/dedicated/private. We also focus on cost controls and rollouts.
[04:47] Priya Shah: One gotcha we hit elsewhere was KV cache invalidation when users change context frequently — how does Redwood handle hot cache churn?
[04:56] Diego Martinez: Good question. The runtime has configurable TTLs for KV cache and our routing can fallback to fresh model variants if cache hits are stale. We'll include an ops note about cache tuning.
[05:08] Sophie Chen: Ok, real quick let's capture concrete next steps: we'll provision free credits for your account, Sophie to send pricing and compliance docs, Diego to run benchmarks once Priya shares prompts, Marco to confirm VPC details.
[05:22] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. Timeline — we're aiming to have an internal demo next Thursday and a decision by end of month depending on bench results.
[05:30] Sophie Chen: Great. We'll aim to get the follow-ups out in 48 hours.
[05:34] Priya Shah: Quick PSA — our legal will likely ask for DPA and standard data processing terms.
[05:40] Sophie Chen: Noted, I'll include our DPA and contact for legal.
[05:44] Marco Ruiz: One small nit — is there a sandbox for trying VPC connectors or is that only for Dedicated customers?
[05:51] Diego Martinez: We can simulate VPC flows for evaluation, but the full private network path is usually in Dedicated/Private onboarding. We'll document the simulated flow.
[06:02] Sophie Chen: Any final questions?
[06:05] Liam O'Connor: None from me. Thanks folks.
[06:08] Priya Shah: Thanks.
[06:10] Sophie Chen: Thanks everyone — recap will be in my follow-up with links: quickstart guide (https://redwood.example/quickstart), SOC2 pack (link), benchmark template (link to spreadsheet), and I'll attach sample PRs for onboarding.
[06:24] Diego Martinez: Quick note — if you want faster turn on Dedicated, we can provision a small reserved pool for benching as an interim.
[06:31] Marco Ruiz: Appreciate it.
[06:34] Sophie Chen: Alright, bye all.
[06:36] Speaker 1 (automated): [call ended]
